title: G4 (Major): UV/IR separation (R3) is not shown to be well-defined

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Theorem `thm:regions` and the "Correct UV/IR labelling" clause of `thm:reduction`.

The problem statement explicitly stresses thermal sum-integrals "mix ultraviolet and infrared divergent regions in a nontrivial way." A single $\varepsilon^{-1}$ pole of a sum-integral can receive contributions from both a UV subregion and an IR region (e.g. 2-loop thermal self-energies with a UV subdivergence overlapping the $n=0$ zero-mode IR divergence).

- The claim that *every* pole produced in sector decomposition carries an *unambiguous* UV-or-IR tag given by "the sign of the scaling exponent of $\lambda$ on the facet" is unjustified: distinct facets/regions can each contribute to the coefficient of the *same* $\varepsilon^{-1}$, so the physical UV-vs-IR split of a pole coefficient is a scheme choice, not a polytope sign. The solution conflates "which region" with "UV vs IR" — not the same dichotomy (a region can be UV in one subloop and IR in another).
- "$x_i\to0$ ⇒ UV, $x_i\to\infty$ ⇒ IR" is a heuristic depending on the parametrization and on which Symanzik factor the variable sits in; it is not uniformly true after blow-ups.

Requirement (R3) demands a genuine separation. A defensible fix needs an **intrinsic definition** of "UV pole" vs "IR pole" of a sum-integral (e.g. via the $R^*$/forest operation, or scaling $\mathbf p\to\Lambda\mathbf p$) and a proof that the region tag computes exactly that, with explicit subtraction handling of the genuinely mixed poles.
